entities.summary:
Lysicles, an Athenian general and prominent leader of the democratic faction, emerged as a significant, albeit short-lived, figure in the turbulent political landscape of Athens during the Peloponnesian War. Active in the mid-fifth century BCE, his career spanned a critical juncture following the death of the influential statesman Pericles in 429 BCE. Lysicles is primarily remembered for his military commands and his association with the radical democratic elements that sought to maintain and extend Periclean policies, even as the city grappled with the devastations of war and plague. His rise reflects the shifting power dynamics within the Athenian assembly and military command structure, where new leaders stepped into the void left by Pericles.

His military career saw him command Athenian forces in various theaters of the Peloponnesian War. Most notably, in 428/427 BCE, Lysicles led an Athenian expedition to Caria in southwestern Anatolia, aiming to collect tribute from allied and subjugated cities. This campaign, part of Athens' broader strategy to fund its war efforts and assert its dominance over the Delian League, involved both diplomatic pressure and military force. During this expedition, Lysicles and a portion of his troops were ambushed and killed by Carian irregulars and local forces near Myus, a significant setback that underscored the dangers of Athenian imperial overreach and the fierce resistance encountered in the tribute-collecting missions.
